findings.title: Shared local-proxy shape duplicated as inline literal
findings.problem: The daemon info shape { url: string; targetUrl?: string } is declared inline in RoutingInput.localProxy (routing.ts:25) and again as the resolveLocalProxy return type (src/agents/plugins/claude-code-otlp/event-fields/local-proxy.ts:9), against code-quality.md Type Annotations: prefer interface, no inline type literals for shared shapes.
findings.impact: Producer (hook daemon lookup) and consumer (routing proof) have no single named contract, so the two declarations can drift silently; violates a documented project type-safety convention that no lint gate enforces.
findings.recommendation: Export an interface (e.g. LocalProxyInfo { url: string; targetUrl?: string }) from routing.ts, use it for RoutingInput.localProxy, and `import type` it as the return type Promise<LocalProxyInfo | undefined> of resolveLocalProxy in local-proxy.ts.

fix.change: Exported LocalProxy interface from routing.ts; RoutingInput.localProxy and resolveLocalProxy return type now use it
fix.test: n/a (type-only refactor; npx tsc --noEmit and existing routing/claude-code-otlp suites green)

deferred.title: Windows daemon liveness judged by pid alone
deferred.problem: isDaemonAlive returns true on win32 when the pid is alive, so a stale proxy-daemon.json plus a recycled pid could make resolveLocalProxy report a dead daemon's url/targetUrl as live.
deferred.preexisting: isDaemonAlive's win32 pid-only check predates this change; the approved fix mandates readState + isDaemonAlive.
